auditor_value: 1/3 s (a = g/3, v at 1 s = g/3; after the stop, string taut again when v t' − ½g t'² = ½g t'², so t' = v/g = 1/3 s, independent of g)

findings.quote: Assuming the string stays taut and the 1 kg block also stops instantly gives a time of 0 s, missing that unequal speeds on a taut string are impossible.
findings.note: Vague: the clause after 'missing' does not name what the student actually misses, which is that a string can only pull, so stopping the 2 kg block cannot stop the 1 kg block and the string must go slack; as written the reader cannot tell why 'both stop' is wrong.
findings.fix: Assuming the string stays taut so the 1 kg block also stops instantly gives a time of 0 s; this misses that a string cannot push, so the 1 kg block keeps its upward speed and the string goes slack.

notes: Independently: relative displacement −v t' + g t'² = 0 gives t' = v/g = (g/3)/g = 1/3 s for any g. Every equation follows. Mistake entry [1]'s value 2v/g = 2/3 s is computed correctly for the error it names.
